newsitem.title: UK: Europe crude outlook - Brent set to stay tight.
newsitem.headline: Europe crude outlook - Brent set to stay tight.

text.p: Tight December North Sea crude supplies and transatlantic arbitrage opportunities were expected to keep Dated Brent values around their recent high levels this week, traders said.
In the Mediterranean, the potential return of Iraqi crude could keep a lid on high sour prices despite disruptions to Urals supplies from the main Russian export port of Novorossiisk.
Dated Brent rallied strongly last week to a high of 49 cents over January paper, before slipping back to talk around Jan +35/+40 on Monday morning.
While traders did not expect the rally to extend much further, neither do they anticipate a sharp fall.
"Brent is expensive, but it looks tight," said a senior trader for a European major. "In the immediate forward period, I'm cautiously bullish."
With the Brent/WTI spread holding above $1 a barrel on Friday, traders said the transatlantic arbitrage remained viable after two North Sea vessels were fixed to the U.S. last week.
Some dealers expected some Brent cargoes scheduled for end-month loading to be deferred to the New Year, because late December is so heavily nominated.
Other North Sea grades were also seen scarce with just a handful of December-loading cargoes, including Oseberg, Ekofisk and Statfjord, still on the market.
"They're all strong and there's no reason why they shouldn't stay there," a North Sea trader said.

Traders said the end of a nine-day strike by workers at Elf's French refineries looked bullish for the physical crude market in the short term. "It means we shouldn't see many more Elf cargoes offered back onto the market," said a trader. "And it'll take a few days for products to came off again...which is nice for (refining) margins."

Traders were divided over the impact of renewed Iraqi exports on the Mediterranean sour market. Iraq said exports would resume on Tuesday, but on Monday European firms said they had not signed any deals yet.

Any eventual return of Kirkuk crude will be easier to absorb because of maintenance at Russia's main export terminal on the Black Sea. Repairs to the main loading berth at Novorossiisk started on Monday and were due to last most of December. In addition, the port was closed by bad weather on Sunday night.

But any Iraqi exports should ensure that Russia's Urals climbs no higher than its current level of Dated Brent -15 cents cif Med, and some Med refiners argued that weak margins should bring sours under pressure.
Mediterranean refiners said West African grades gave a margin of 50/60 cents a barrel over Urals. "Urals is going to weaken to around (Dated Brent) -40/50 cents," said one refiner.
With few December barrels left, sweet West African grades could attract even stronger premiums this week, with Bonny Light well bid in the mid-60s over Dated Brent, traders said.
